units.title: The Subject Matter of Geography
units.intro: Geography studies the Earth as the home of people — **where** things are and **why** they are there. Two big halves: **physical** (land, weather, water, living cover) and **human** (population, settlements, economy). Modern fields: geomorphology, climatology, biogeography, economic, population, political, cartography. The glue is **spatial** thinking: location, place, region, movement, human–environment.

cards.title: 1.1 Understanding Geography
body: Sub-unit 1.1 presents the definition of geography and discusses its importance in providing basic knowledge about the world.
The sub-unit also presents the history of geography in brief.
Geography is the study of the earth and its lands, features, inhabitants and phenomena.

The word geography comes from a Greek word that means “earth description.” Studying how things are organized on the earth provides useful information to understand environmental changes caused by people.
Problems related to food supply, the environment or development can also be easily understood through geographic knowledge and skills.

cards.title: Worked from review
cards.problem: Who is historically recognized as the "father of geography as well as history"?

steps.text: **Step 1: Identify the historical scholar who integrated human events with geography.**
Herodotus was an ancient Greek scholar who described both the physical environments and local human cultures of his era.
Because of his double emphasis on chronological history and spatial descriptions, he is celebrated as the father of both disciplines.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which ancient scholar analyzed physical atmospheric processes such as temperature and wind?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall the contributions of Aristotle to physical sciences.**
Aristotle investigated natural systems and was interested in how temperature and winds operate globally.

**Step 2: Align with geographic branches.**
His systematic examination of meteorological phenomena laid the foundation for physical geography.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct answer is **Aristotle**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The Greek scholar who measured the Earth's circumference and first used the word 'geography' was:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the scholar who measured the Earth's size mathematically.**
Eratosthenes of Cyrene, living in Alexandria, utilized solar angles on the summer solstice to determine the Earth's circumference.

**Step 2: Identify who coined the term.**
He is also globally recognized as the individual who coined the word "geography."

**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct option is **Eratosthenes**.

cards.title: Quick check

cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the historical scholar who integrated human events with geography.**
Herodotus was an ancient Greek scholar who described both the physical environments and local human cultures of his era.

**Step 2: Match his titles.**
Because of his double emphasis on chronological history and spatial descriptions, he is celebrated as the father of both disciplines.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Thus, the correct scholar is **Herodotus**.

cards.title: 1.2 Fields of Modern Geography
body: Modern geography is unique as it studies the world from at different points including both man-made and natural features of the earth’s surface.

For example, a geographer who studies the growing of wheat in a particular region needs information on the climate, soil and landform of the region as well as knowledge about the transport network and the price of wheat.
Geographers today not only describe things, but they also attempt to explain why things are distributed over the earth as they are.
Human Geography: Human geography is the study of the relationships between human beings and the natural environment.
Human geography covers a number of fields.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In which century BC did Eratosthenes adopt the term 'geography' and calculate the Earth's size?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the historical date associated with Eratosthenes' work.**
Eratosthenes conducted his calculations during the 3rd century BC, which is chronologically represented by the 200s BC.

**Step 2: Recall the key facts.**
The text explicitly states that the term was adopted in the "200s BC."

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct choice is **2nd century BC (200s BC)**.

glossary.meaning: Human Geography: Human geography is the study of the relationships between human beings and the natural environment.
Physical Geography: Physical geography is the study of the natural environment from the perspective of distribution and process.
In other words, regional geography is the study of environmental and human features within a single area.
Geography is the study of the earth and its lands, features, inhabitants and phenomena.

tips.text: Geography is a science that deals with the distribution and arrangement of all elements of the earth’s surface.

Geographic study encompasses the environment of the earth’s surface and the relationship of humans beingse to their environment which includes both physical and human geography.
Modern geography studies the world from different point of views. It studies man-made environment, natural environment and the interrelationship between humans beingse and their environment.
